cases.title: The Quiet Child
cases.presentation: Apartment collapse. You find a ~5-year-old boy lying still, not breathing. You reposition his airway — still no breathing. You feel a weak radial pulse.
cases.question: Per JumpSTART, what do you do?
options: A: Tag delayed and return later.
C: Tag deceased and move on.
D: Give 5 rescue breaths (~15 s): if he breathes → IMMEDIATE; if not → DECEASED.
cases.explanation: Pediatric arrests are often respiratory; a child with a pulse may respond to ventilation alone. JumpSTART spends 15 seconds on 5 breaths — never full CPR.
cases.clinicalPearl: Pulse + apnea in a child = 5 breaths before black.

cases.title: Thirty on the Dot
cases.presentation: Train derailment. A man pinned by the legs (can't walk) is breathing 30/min, radial pulse strong, CRT 1.5 s, and answers 'yes' when asked to squeeze your hand — and does it.
cases.question: START category?
options: C: DELAYED — RR is not > 30, perfusion and mental status OK.
cases.explanation: START's cut-off is RR MORE than 30. He passes all three checks → Delayed. Re-triage: entrapment can become crush syndrome.

cases.title: Green Who Turned Gray-Skinned
cases.presentation: 45 minutes after a bus crash, a woman tagged GREEN at the walking-wounded point is now pale, sweaty, and says she feels faint. She has left-upper-quadrant abdominal pain.
cases.question: What does this teach?
options: A: Walkers can hide internal bleeding — re-triage greens; she now meets IMMEDIATE criteria (perfusion).
cases.explanation: START sorts by snapshot physiology. A splenic injury may present late. Re-triage the green area regularly with a medic assigned.
cases.clinicalPearl: Greens need a babysitter with a stethoscope.

cases.title: Thirty-Second Challenge
cases.presentation: You've tagged 9 patients in 6 minutes. The 10th, a middle-aged woman, is screaming with an open tib-fib fracture, RR 26, radial pulse strong, follows commands perfectly, bleeding is oozing (not arterial).
cases.question: What's your tag and how long should it take?
options: B: Splint first, then tag — 3 minutes.
C: IMMEDIATE because of the open fracture.
D: DELAYED — tag in ~30 s; she's loud but physiologically stable; move on.
cases.explanation: Noise and gore don't change START categories. She passes RPM → Delayed. The silent patient behind her may be the red.
cases.clinicalPearl: Loud is alive — go find the quiet ones.
